description.text: Our mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly. Aurora was founded in 2017 by Chris Urmson, Sterling Anderson, and Drew Bagnell, three of the most prominent leaders in the self-driving space. Led by a team with deep experience, including Chris and Drew, we have launched and are continuing to develop the Aurora Driver based on what we believe to be the most advanced and scalable suite of self-driving hardware, software, and data services in the world to fundamentally transform the global transportation market. The Aurora Driver is designed as a platform to adapt and interoperate amongst a multitude of vehicle types and applications. To date, we have successfully integrated the Aurora Driver into numerous different vehicle platforms designed to meet its requirements: from passenger vehicles to light commercial vehicles to Class 8 trucks. By creating a common driver platform for multiple vehicle types and use cases, the capabilities we develop in one market reinforce and strengthen our competitive advantages in other areas. For example, highway driving capabilities developed for trucking will carry over to highway segments driven by passenger vehicles in ride hailing applications. We believe this is the right approach to bring self-driving to market and will enable us to target and transform multiple massive markets, including trucking, passenger mobility, and local goods delivery.

about.description_short: Aurora (Nasdaq: AUR) is delivering the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly to make transportation safer, increasingly accessible, and more reliable and efficient than ever before. The Aurora Driver is a self-driving system designed to operate multiple vehicle types, from freight-hauling trucks to ride-hailing passenger vehicles, and underpins Aurora's driver as a service product for trucking. Aurora is working with industry leaders across the transportation ecosystem, including AUMOVIO, FedEx, Hirschbach, McLane, NVIDIA, PACCAR, Ryder, Schneider, Toyota, Uber, Uber Freight, Volvo Trucks, Volvo Autonomous Solutions, and Werner.

analysis_md:
# AUR — Aurora Innovation, Inc.
Engine 5.4 run, 2026-10-18. In scope (market cap $8.928B at $4.855, nasdaq_quote_api — engine figure).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, financials_history.csv, ttm.py output, fundamentals.json, or the cited Q2 2026 reporting — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Autonomous trucking: the Aurora Driver (hardware + software stack) sold mainly as Driver-as-a-Service per mile, integrated factory-side by PACCAR (Peterbilt/Kenworth) and Volvo, with an asset-light model where customers own the trucks. First commercial driverless operations on U.S. public roads began on Dallas–Houston in spring 2025; by the September 23, 2026 Investor Day the company reported more than 500,000 driverless miles, targets exiting 2026 with 200 driverless trucks and more than 1,000 at end-2027, guides FY2026 revenue of $14–16M (~400% growth at the midpoint, back-loaded to Q4), and frames a 2030 vision of 30,000+ trucks, more than $5B revenue and ~60% gross margin, with positive free cash flow targeted in 2028. Today it is pre-commercial in every financial sense: Q2 2026 revenue was $2M against a $266M operating loss.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow −$581,000,000; capex $31,000,000; SBC $188,000,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$800,000,000 = −$0.44/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share −0.43501903208265363).
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): −$863,000,000 — also deeply negative; the two definitions agree on sign and rough size.
- **OE positive in 0 of the last 5 fiscal years.** Normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share) = **−$0.49/share** (base_oe_normalized_per_share −0.48763906056860323) — the base used, because it is the engine standard and every alternative base is also negative (see STALE_FY). No scenario DCF is supportable: the engine emits no IV or IRR for any scenario when the normalized base is negative, and the tier is F by definition (no positive conservative owner's earnings). F sub-type: no_cash_generation — OCF − capex is not positive over the median window.
- Balance sheet (see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK): total liabilities were only $203,000,000 at FY2025 end against assets of $2,343,000,000 and equity of $2,140,000,000 — this is an equity-funded company with minimal leverage, not a debt problem. Liquidity at Q2 2026 was nearly $1.2B in cash and short-term investments after a $215M at-the-market raise in the quarter — but at a guided $190–220M of quarterly cash use, that is roughly five to six quarters of runway, so the cash pile is burn funding, not excess capital.

## Moat: 3/10 — weak, a first-mover lead that has not yet become a franchise
Justification: first-mover commercial lead, a clean safety record (500,000+ driverless miles, zero Aurora-attributed collisions), and factory integration with PACCAR and Volvo are real assets, but the fleet is ~200 trucks targeted by end-2026 so no scale/network effect exists, funded rivals are deploying (Volvo also partners with Waabi), Aurora owns neither trucks nor freight demand, and the measured economics are deeply negative — roic_proxy from fundamentals.json was −33.3% (2021), −96.1% (2022), −44.5% (2023), −37.3% (2024) and −37.1% (2025), with gross margin unfiled in most pre-revenue years and −466.7% in FY2025 (gross profit −$14,000,000 on $3,000,000 revenue). A moat of 7+ needs ROIC well above the cost of capital through a cycle; Aurora has never printed a positive year.
- FOR: First commercial driverless trucking on US public roads (Dallas–Houston, 2025); 500,000+ driverless miles with zero Aurora-attributed collisions; factory OEM integration with PACCAR (Peterbilt/Kenworth) and Volvo — together roughly half the US Class 8 market; Aurora Driver data flywheel — every driverless mile trains a system later rivals lack; customer/partner web: Hirschbach (500-truck Driver-as-a-Service plan from 2027), McLane, Schneider, Uber Freight, FedEx.
- AGAINST: Fleet still tiny (200 trucks targeted by end-2026) — no scale or network effect yet; funded rivals deploying: Kodiak, Waabi (also a Volvo partner), PlusAI, Tesla; owns neither the trucks nor the freight demand — customers can switch autonomy suppliers; no pricing power or returns proven (ROIC proxy negative every year since 2021, FY2025 gross margin −466.7%); continuous dilution funds the buildout — share count +17.2%/yr, SBC $205M TTM and rising.
- A 3 gives CAP = 5.9 years — moot here, since there is no positive base OE to project.

## DCF — engine 5.4 final run (2026-10-18)
Final engine pass run with --moat 3 --probs 0.10/0.25/0.30/0.25/0.10 (defaults retained; offsets/multipliers not applicable). Price $4.855.
- **No scenario table exists for this name, by design:** with normalized base OE of −$0.49/share, latest-FY −$0.44/share, and TTM −$0.49/share, the engine produces no IV@15% and no implied IRR in any scenario — super bear through super bull all scale a negative base. Growth optics are equally unusable: revenue CAGR 5y/3y −26.86% and latest YoY −95.59% are artifacts of pilot/collaboration revenue winding to zero before the driverless business started (see BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT); FY2025 revenue was $3,000,000 against $581,000,000 of operating cash burn.
- **Tier by numbers: F** (f_subtype: no_cash_generation). Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not emitted (null in dcf_numbers.json).
- Diagnostics: OE positive 0/5 years; share count CAGR 17.17%/yr; lease liabilities $84,000,000; net debt not computable from filed debt tags (see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK).

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (FY ended 2025-12-31, ~10 months ago): resolved with ttm.py, whose full output is saved in ttm.json. TTM inputs (FY − prior YTD + current YTD, current YTD ended 2026-06-30): OCF FY −$581,000,000, prior YTD −$286,000,000, current YTD −$384,000,000 → TTM −$679,000,000. Capex FY $31,000,000, prior YTD $15,000,000, current YTD $56,000,000 → TTM $72,000,000. SBC FY $188,000,000, prior YTD $89,000,000, current YTD $106,000,000 → TTM $205,000,000. Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted) 1,962,000,000. **TTM OE total −$956,000,000 → −$0.49/share** (ttm_oe_per_share −0.4872579001019368) — effectively identical to the normalized base (−$0.49/share), so the F verdict does not depend on base choice and no --ttm pin was applied.
- **DILUTION** (share count +17.17%/yr): real and structural. Diluted shares per the filed history: 1,327,000,000 (FY2023) → 1,618,000,000 (FY2024) → 1,839,000,000 (FY2025) → 1,962,000,000 (current YTD 2026, ttm.py). SBC compounds with it — $160,000,000 (FY2023), $144,000,000 (FY2024), $188,000,000 (FY2025), $205,000,000 TTM (ttm.py legs above) — and the burn is equity-financed directly: in Q2 2026 alone the company issued 30,000,000 shares through its at-the-market program for $215,000,000 net, and fundamentals.json records $736,000,000 of share issuance over the TTM window. At guided quarterly cash use of $190–220M against nearly $1.2B of liquidity, further raises before the targeted 2028 positive free cash flow are unavoidable; any future positive OE will be divided by a much larger share count than today's.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump/drop in last 5 yrs): not a divestiture, M&A, or restatement — it is pre-commercial revenue lumpiness. Filed revenue was $82,000,000 (FY2021) and $68,000,000 (FY2022) from early pilot/collaboration activity, then $0 in FY2023 and FY2024 as those programs wound down, then $3,000,000 in FY2025 as the new driverless freight revenue started from zero after the spring-2025 commercial launch (TTM revenue $5,000,000 per fundamentals.json). Every revenue CAGR in dcf_numbers.json (−26.86% 5y/3y, latest YoY −95.59%) is therefore an artifact and was not used for any growth input — there is no growth input to make, since the base OE is negative.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025): net income −$816,000,000 vs operating cash flow −$581,000,000 — a $235,000,000 gap explained almost entirely by non-cash charges added back in the cash-flow statement: SBC $188,000,000 plus D&A $30,000,000 (both from financials_history.csv) account for $218,000,000 of it, with the remainder in working-capital/other items. There is no one-off flattering either figure. The conservative OE base is built from OCF and deducts SBC separately, so the divergence does not contaminate the base — the F rests on the cash burn itself, not on this gap.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt UNKNOWN, not zero): stated from the filing instead. The FY2025 balance sheet in financials_history.csv shows total assets $2,343,000,000, total liabilities $203,000,000, equity $2,140,000,000, and lease liabilities of $84,000,000 (the only leverage-like line the engine found, via OperatingLeaseLiability tags). A company carrying only $203M of total liabilities on a $2,343M balance sheet has no material funded debt whether or not a debt tag prints; it is financed by equity, and company reporting at Q2 2026 put cash and short-term investments at nearly $1.2B. The leverage verdict is therefore: effectively unlevered, with liquidity — not solvency — as the binding constraint (see DILUTION for runway).

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is a venture-stage autonomy bet trading at $8.928B. The OE-DCF has nothing to grip: five straight years of negative owner's earnings on both definitions, every base at −$0.44 to −$0.49/share, and TTM operating cash burn of $679,000,000 against TTM revenue of $5,000,000.
- The bull case is not a DCF case: if the fleet scales 200 → 1,000+ → 30,000 trucks and per-mile Driver-as-a-Service economics reach the guided ~60% gross margin, today's financials are irrelevant. That outcome is binary on second-generation hardware cost, OEM production cadence, regulatory breadth, safety record survival — and on capital markets staying open for the ~5–6 quarters of runway left before the 2027–2028 revenue ramp.
- There is no hurdle-clearing price to quote: with negative owner's earnings at every base, no positive price produces a 15% OE-implied return. The 15% question only becomes askable after the company prints its first positive-OE year; until then any entry price is paying for the option, not the cash flows.
- Sizing: the F is a statement about the screen, not a short thesis — pre-revenue compounders fail this screen by construction. But on Andrew's hurdles there is nothing here to underwrite today.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (no positive normalized owner's earnings — 0/5 years, every base negative: median −$0.49, latest FY −$0.44, TTM −$0.49 per share; f_subtype no_cash_generation)
- Confidence: **Medium** (the F arithmetic is unambiguous on filed data; anything forward-looking about this name is binary on scaling execution and financing, so the overall call is not high-confidence)
- One-liner: Pre-commercial autonomous-trucking leader, moat 3/10, but owner's earnings are negative on every base (TTM −$0.49/sh, 0/5 years positive) and the ~$200M/quarter burn is funded by dilution (+17.2%/yr share count) — no positive price clears the 15% hurdle until it prints a positive-OE year.
